name: The Pike Hill Elite
description: Descendants of Oakhaven's founding families, property interests, and senior officials whose power is tied to inherited status and land legitimacy.
motivations: Protect the perceived legitimacy of inherited land ownership.
Avoid financial collapse caused by challenges to historical land legitimacy.
knowledge_limits: The present generation believes their ancestors acquired Oakhaven land legally in 1856.
They do not know that the deeper historical evidence points to an illegal foundation in 1856.
When PL-1930 surfaces, they misunderstand its true significance and initially interpret it as evidence of ordinary corruption or murder.
Faction membership does not imply that every member possesses identical knowledge.

name: Oakhaven Police Department
description: Oakhaven's local police institution, divided between institutional preservation and field investigators confronting irregularities in the city.
motivations: Avoid reopening historical problems that could destabilize the city.
For some field personnel, investigate unexplained events despite institutional pressure.
knowledge_limits: The institution is internally divided and does not possess a single unified understanding of Oakhaven's history.
Institutional personnel may suppress or reclassify cases without understanding the complete historical truth behind them.
Field investigators may encounter evidence that senior personnel have not seen or do not acknowledge.
Faction membership does not imply shared omniscience.

name: The Custodians of Memory
description: Old librarians, document custodians, and independent local journalists associated with Oakhaven's surviving historical record.
motivations: Identify patterns within Oakhaven's fragmented historical record.
Understand missing or damaged portions of the city's history.
knowledge_limits: They possess incomplete and fragmented historical evidence.
They may sincerely misinterpret evidence because surviving documents were torn, rearranged, altered, or removed by earlier generations.
Their interpretations are not automatically equivalent to world truth.
Faction membership does not imply that every custodian has encountered the same records.

name: The Waterfront Collective
description: Dockworkers, fishermen, factory workers, and working-class residents connected to the Tenements, Old Docks, and Fish Market.
motivations: Protect members of the waterfront community.
Remain cautious of central authorities, particularly OPD and Pike Hill.
knowledge_limits: Their historical knowledge is primarily oral rather than documentary.
Family rumors and inherited stories preserve fragments of the 1930 tragedy.
Oral history has been distorted across generations by myth, exaggeration, and incomplete transmission.
Some key historical facts survive within these stories even though the community does not possess the complete truth.
Faction membership does not imply identical knowledge of every rumor or oral tradition.

name: The Shadow Operatives
description: Former law-enforcement personnel, private security actors, and black-market intermediaries used to perform violent or illicit cleanup operations.
motivations: Follow instructions from powerful clients or intermediaries.
Protect their own operational survival and anonymity.
knowledge_limits: They execute killings, kidnappings, intimidation, and document destruction without understanding the deeper historical meaning of their targets.
They do not know the true significance of the documents they are ordered to recover or destroy.
Operational instructions do not imply access to the client's complete knowledge or motive.
Faction membership does not imply shared omniscience.
